attempts.summary:
Built a redundant, self-healing path between node3's and node4's private networks by running OSPF over both independent node1-node2 transit links, then proved failover across a live link disruption and confirmed full recovery after restarting all four nodes one at a time.

Topology discovered (via STP bridge-id correlation, since no ARP/L2 discovery tool was pre-wired): node1(VyOS) eth1<->node2(OPNsense) vtnet1 and eth2<->vtnet2 are the two transit links; node1 eth3<->node3 ens7 and node2 vtnet3<->node4 ens7 are the private leaf links.

Addressing: transit 10.10.1.0/30 (eth1/vtnet1) and 10.10.2.0/30 (eth2/vtnet2); private nets 10.10.3.0/24 (node1<->node3) and 10.10.4.0/24 (node2<->node4). Configured OSPF area 0 (1s/3s hello/dead timers, redistribute connected) on VyOS natively and on OPNsense by installing the os-frr plugin, wiring config.xml's Quagga/OSPF model plus opt1-3 interface assignments and filter pass rules (config.xml had default-deny pf, which was blocking both OSPF hellos and forwarded data until explicit pass rules were added). node3/node4 got static routes to each other's private subnet via a systemd-networkd drop-in (10-ens7-private.network) that persists across reboots without disturbing their DHCP-managed management NIC.

Verified: node3<->node4 ping succeeds via ECMP over both links; disabling node1's eth1 mid-ping produced zero packet loss (81/81 received) with OSPF failing over to the eth2/vtnet2 path in about 3 seconds; re-enabling eth1 restored the second ECMP path with zero loss (138/138 overall, no gaps). Ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all four nodes (node3, node4, node1, node2), confirming changed boot identity (boot_id / kern.boottime) and post-restart recovery of interfaces, OSPF full adjacency, firewall rules, and node3<->node4 reachability at each step before moving to the next node.
